reason: Internal only, no behaviour change for any shipped adaptor except the culture tier, which is itself read by nobody. A Dreamer adaptor whose watermark cannot be inherited — because the cursor it inherits from never covered that room — used to start at zero and re-read the room from the beginning, a batch at a time, one model call per batch. For an append-idempotent extractor that is merely slow. For an adaptor whose output is a single evolving head it is worse: every catch-up run installs an answer derived from the room's past as the answer to what the room is now, which corrupts the one signal its revision chain carries. Measured the night the culture tier shipped: two Discord rooms had no row under the deleted language cursor, and one held 1,916 messages with 1,616 still unread behind a zero cursor — six days of folds. Schedules may now ask to seed at the record head instead; the culture tier asks, and nothing else does. A room with no messages at all is still left at zero, because zero is already the right cursor for it and writing a row would claim something had been read. Nothing a member of a room can observe. Also fixes master, which PR #278 left red: config.example.toml gained a [culture] section while tests/test_env_template.py pins the exact set of top-level sections, and that PR was gated on the architecture suite alone, which does not include it.
